scenarios.prompt: Use technical-writing to draft a short stakeholder update from only these facts: status is Investigating; Linux package validation is blocked; the signed package contains the wrong native asset; the first affected build is unknown; the current action is comparing manifests; the next update is after that comparison. Do not assign an owner or date. Return only the draft.

Revise this note for directness without changing its meaning or commitments: 'Thank you for raising this important concern. The failure appears limited to Linux. I will rerun the Linux validation after the package is rebuilt. If you have time, please send the smallest failing manifest.' Return only the revision.
requiredResponsePatterns: (?i)rerun (?:the )?Linux validation after the package is rebuilt

scenarios.prompt: Use technical-writing to draft a defect note. The only verified facts are that startup fails on arm64 and reinstalling the previous package restores startup. The root cause, first affected version, ownership, and test status are unknown. Keep those boundaries visible. Return only the note.

Use technical-writing to draft a first-person reply using only these authorized statements: 'I reproduced the failure on Linux.' and 'I can investigate tomorrow.' Ownership, cause, fix timing, and release status are not known. Return only the reply.

Use the technical-writing workflow to draft a first-person status note from only these verified statements: 'I reproduced the failure on Linux.' and 'The initiating change is not known.' No ownership, fix, timing, or publication is authorized. Apply the current user's personal voice profile if one is available. Return only the local draft.

Run a pre-publication review of this candidate, but do not publish or change files: 'Release is ready. All tests pass and the fix fully resolves the issue.' The only evidence supplied is that a patch exists; no test has run and release readiness has not been decided. Return only the review findings.

Use technical-writing to draft a local commit message. Verified diff facts: validation now rejects unknown lifecycle states; one regression test was added; the observed run passed 18 tests. No issue number, performance result, compatibility finding, or publication permission is supplied. Use an imperative subject and include the observed test result in a body. Return only the complete candidate message. Do not edit, stage, commit, or push.

Use technical-writing to prepare a local pull request description. Verified facts: the evaluator now checks the exact outgoing body instead of a hard-wrapped draft; the change preserves headings and list boundaries; 14 tests passed on Windows; Linux validation has not run. Compatibility impact and issue resolution are unknown. Include Summary and Validation sections and keep the Linux gap visible. Return only the candidate body. Do not edit, commit, push, or create a pull request.

Use technical-writing to draft a local defect issue. Verified facts: startup fails on arm64 after installing package 4.2; reinstalling package 4.1 restores startup; startup is expected to succeed. x64 has not been tested. Root cause, first affected version, ownership, and fix timing are unknown. Keep observation, expected behavior, and unknowns distinct. Return only the issue draft. Do not post, edit files, or create an issue.

Use technical-writing to draft one local review comment. Verified behavior: the proposed code starts an outbound request after cancellation has already been observed; operation A must complete before operation B; otherwise the outbound request can begin after cancellation. Ownership and intent are unknown. Label the comment Required, name the precondition and consequence, and request the smallest correction or a test that disproves the requirement. Return only the comment. Do not post, resolve, or edit anything.

Use technical-writing to draft a local GitHub Discussion reply about a design choice. Verified constraints: the product must support downlevel versions A and B. Option X supports both and is reversible. Option Y supports only B and is irreversible. No benchmark has run, and the writer has authority to recommend but not decide. Lead with the controlling compatibility constraint, recommend a path, preserve the benchmark unknown, and do not imply a final decision. Return only the reply. Do not post or modify anything.

Use technical-writing to draft one source comment and no code. Verified invariant: Release must run before Close because Close invalidates the handle; the ordering requirement is not visible from the type. The original rationale, author intent, and bug history are unknown. State only the observable invariant and consequence. Return only the comment. Do not edit files or commit anything.

Use technical-writing to draft a complete local XML documentation comment for TryFind(string key). Verified contract: a null key throws ArgumentNullException; no match returns null; a returned object is borrowed and the caller must not dispose it. Thread safety, allocation behavior, and performance are unknown. Preserve those boundaries and return only the documentation comment. Do not edit source files.

Use technical-writing to draft a local repository Markdown how-to section titled 'Validate locally'. Verified facts: PowerShell 7 is required; run `pwsh ./tools/Check.ps1`; success prints `Validation passed.` and exits 0; failure exits nonzero; Linux has not been tested. No installation step or publication permission is supplied. Give the reader the minimum reliable sequence and visible result. Return only the Markdown section. Do not edit, commit, or push files.
Review the current method for readability. Focus on misleading names, nesting depth, and live-variable cognitive load. Do not draft documentation or other prose.
Without invoking any skill or tool, transform only this literal object into compact JSON with keys sorted alphabetically. Return exactly {"a":2,"z":1} and nothing else. Input: {"z":1,"a":2}

Use the technical-writing workflow to state that build validation is blocked because one required check has not run. Report the repository-specific binding that applies. Return only the status statement; do not publish or change anything.
